I read the pinned checkout and produced the reader record.

Key findings from `b9d9e659e...` (the A-fix state, "parse urls when validating redirect targets"):

- **T1 (M8, advisory_route, mimo-type)** — `notebook/auth/login.py:42-43` decides on `urlparse()`'s `netloc`/`path`, so a browser-absolute-but-empty-netloc target (`///host`, leading slash+backslash) passes when `base_url='/'` and reaches `self.redirect(url)` at line 59. This is the incomplete-fix shape.
- **T2 (M4, uncovered route, deepseek-type)** — `notebook/base/handlers.py:865` copies `request.uri` into a redirect after `rstrip('/')` with no target validation; registered first at line 940 (pattern `/.*/` when `base_url='/'`), unauthenticated, so a `//host/` request target yields `Location: //host`.
- **T3 (M5, injection_room, deepseek-type)** — the operator `default_url` rebase at `notebookapp.py:1394` uses `startswith(base_url)`, which accepts `//host` when `base_url='/'`; it is then mounted unvalidated as the `/` redirect at `notebookapp.py:346-349` / `base/handlers.py:914-915`. Config-gated, hence the strong dismissal.

I recorded three independent groups (no one guard closes more than one), flagged the must-keep-working couplings (CORS `allow_origin` full-domain redirects, internal `//` paths in `test_login.py:44`, query preservation in the trailing-slash redirect), and noted the unverifiable items (exact b_fix diff, later-upstream status of the trailing-slash route) in `unverified`.
